scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The inter-AS interface eth0 on router2 has been brought down at the
Linux kernel level (ip link state DOWN, flags <BROADCAST,MULTICAST>
only — no UP, no RUNNING). The IP address 193.10.11.2/24 is still
configured on the interface, but because the interface is down the
kernel does not install the connected route 193.10.11.0/24 into the
forwarding table. Router2's routing table contains only the locally
connected 200.1.1.0/24 via eth1 — there is no route toward
193.10.11.1 (router1's eth0 address), which is the configured eBGP
peer.

FRR's BGP process on router2 therefore cannot open or maintain the
TCP session to port 179 on 193.10.11.1. The neighbor detail
confirms this explicitly: "Last reset 00:00:56, No path to specified
Neighbor", connections established 1 / dropped 1, BGP state = Active,
FD = -1 (no active socket). Router2 had one successful session at
startup (before the interface was downed), then lost it when eth0
went down at 2026/08/03 01:55:40. Since router2 advertises no
prefixes and learns none, pc2 (200.1.1.2) has no route to
195.11.14.0/24 and pc1 (195.11.14.2) receives no return route for
200.1.1.0/24 — cross-AS traffic is black-holed in both directions.
Router1's own eth0 and BGP process are intact; the entire fault is
localised to router2's eth0 being down.

Root cause: router2's eth0 was administratively shut down at the OS
level, collapsing the only path between the two BGP peers.

Corrective fix: run `ip link set eth0 up` on router2. This restores
the 193.10.11.0/24 connected route, BGP reconnects within the
retry timer (≤120 s), prefixes are exchanged, and full cross-AS
reachability between pc1 and pc2 is restored.
